overview.intro:
Chapter 67 covers **wigs, hair extensions and false eyelashes** (6704), **worked human hair** (6703), **artificial flowers, foliage and fruit** (6702) and **prepared feathers, down and feather articles** (6701). Its **13 tariff lines** split in two: every hair, wig and extension line is **Free**, while artificial flowers pay 3.4%–17% and feather goods 4.7%.

The extra duty by country decides the cost. Since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%** — 10% from Indonesia, Bangladesh and India, 12.5% from Vietnam — and no Chapter 67 line is exempt. **China pays 20% on synthetic wigs and 12.5% on human-hair wigs**, 15.9%–37% on artificial flowers and 42.2% on feather goods. Senegal and Myanmar are outside the 60, so their wigs enter Free. U.S. imports were **$2.14B in 2025**, 74% from China.

workedExamples.title: Synthetic lace-front wigs: China vs Indonesia vs Myanmar
workedExamples.body: Complete wigs of synthetic fibers are Free at the general rate. The line was only on China's suspended List 4B, so Chinese extensions pay just the 12.5% 2026 duty: **$1,250** on $10,000. Indian extensions pay 10%: **$1,000**. Extensions made in China from Indian-prepared hair are of Indian origin (N349850).

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** This chapter does not cover: (a) filtering or straining cloth of human hair (heading 5911); (b) floral motifs of lace, of embroidery or other textile fabric (section XI); (c) footwear (chapter 64); (d) headgear or hair-nets (chapter 65); (e) toys, sports equipment, or carnival articles (chapter 95); or (f) feather dusters, powder-puffs or hair sieves (chapter 96).

**Note 2.** Heading 6701 does not cover: (a) articles in which feathers or down constitute only filling or padding (for example, bedding of heading 9404); (b) articles of apparel or clothing accessories in which feathers or down constitute no more than mere trimming, filling or padding; or (c) artificial flowers or foliage or parts thereof or made up articles of heading 6702.

**Note 3.** Heading 6702 does not cover: (a) articles of glass (chapter 70); or (b) artificial flowers, foliage or fruit of pottery, stone, metal, wood or other materials, obtained in one piece by molding, forging, carving, stamping or other process, or consisting of parts assembled otherwise than by binding, gluing, fitting into one another or similar methods.

tariffUpdates.h1: HTS Chapter 67 Tariff Updates: Wigs, Hair Extensions, Artificial Flowers & Feathers (2025–2026)

seo.title: HTS Chapter 67 Tariff Updates 2026: Wigs, Human Hair & Artificial Flowers — Section 301, IEEPA End | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What changed for HTS Chapter 67 wigs, hair extensions, eyelashes, artificial flowers and feather articles since January 2025: unchanged base rates, the IEEPA tariffs and their end, the Section 122 surcharge, the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on Indonesia, Vietnam and India, China's List 3 and 4A duties and Canada's 50% duty on synthetic hairpieces.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). All 13 Chapter 67 lines carry the same base rates in both — Free on hair, wigs and extensions, 3.4%–17% on artificial flowers and 4.7% on feather goods.

What changed came on top of the base rate. In 2025 the IEEPA tariffs added 19%–20% on Indonesian, Bangladeshi and Vietnamese wigs, 40% on Myanmar's, 25%–50% on Indian hair and 20%–145% more on Chinese goods. They **ended on February 24, 2026**, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026**, goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%**, with no exemption for any Chapter 67 line. China keeps its List 3 (25%) and List 4A (7.5%) duties, and since **August 22, 2026 Canada pays 50%** under Section 338 on synthetic hairpieces (6704.19), USMCA claim or not.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 67 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies, the Brazil Section 301 tariff, China Section 301 Lists 3 and 4A, the Canada Section 338 duty on 6704.19, Russia's rate in lieu of column 2 on human hair, the Nicaragua Section 301 phase-in, and the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended; plus the Section 337 exclusion order on certain pre-stretched synthetic braiding hair. No antidumping or countervailing duty order and no Section 232 action covers a Chapter 67 line. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.exemption: Two Section 301 duties can stack. The 2026 action adds +12.5% (9903.05.31) on all 13 lines. List 3 (+25%, 9903.88.03) covers the two feather lines (6701.00.30, .60); List 4A (+7.5%, 9903.88.15) covers feather flowers (6702.90.10), other artificial flowers (6702.90.65), worked hair (6703.00.30, .60), synthetic wigs and hairpieces (6704.11, 6704.19) and wigs of other materials (6704.90). Plastic flowers (6702.10), man-made-fiber flowers (6702.90.35) and human-hair wigs and extensions (6704.20) were only on List 4B, which USTR suspended in December 2019, so they pay no 2018–2019 duty. No China exclusion now in effect names a Chapter 67 product. USTR confirmed on October 7, 2026 that the 2018–2019 actions continue. The IEEPA duties on China (20% fentanyl, cut to 10% on November 10, 2025, plus 10% reciprocal) ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: No Chapter 67 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 13 Chapter 67 lines carry the same General, FTA and Column 2 rates in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition; no line was added, split or renumbered.

changes.title: China Section 301 Lists 3 and 4A continue
changes.detail: USTR received requests to continue the 2018–2019 China Section 301 actions, so they stay in effect during the four-year review. For Chapter 67 this keeps +25% on feather articles (9903.88.03) and +7.5% on seven hair, wig and flower lines (9903.88.15), on top of the 12.5% 2026 action.

changes.title: Canadian import bans do not reach Chapter 67
changes.detail: Proclamations 11061–11063 banned some Canadian alcoholic beverages, dairy-scope products and motorcycles over 800 cc from September 29, 2026. 6704.19 stays on the 9903.03.14 duty list but is not on a ban annex, so it keeps paying the 50% duty.

changes.title: Section 338 motor-vehicle retaliation list revised; 6704.19 stays on it
changes.detail: Proclamation 11065 modified the list of Canadian products under 9903.03.14 from September 15, 2026. 6704.19 (synthetic hairpieces, extensions and eyelashes) was not removed.

changes.title: Canada Section 338 duty of 50% on 6704.19
changes.detail: Proclamation 11048, which answers Canadian treatment of U.S. motor vehicles, put a 50% duty (9903.03.14) on Canadian goods in the provisions of U.S. note 51(b)(3). The list includes 6704.19: wigs, hairpieces, extensions and false eyelashes of synthetic fibers other than complete wigs. It is charged even when USMCA is claimed and on top of the 10% Section 301 duty on non-USMCA goods. Planned for August 19, it took effect August 22 after a 3-day suspension (Proclamation 11056).

changes.title: Second braiding-hair patent case ends with no violation
changes.detail: The ITC ended Investigation 337-TA-1457 (pre-stretched synthetic braiding hair, II) without finding a violation of Section 337, so no new exclusion order was issued. The September 2025 order from 337-TA-1415 stays in force.

changes.title: UFLPA Entity List updated; Xinjiang hair producers still listed
changes.detail: DHS added more entities to the UFLPA Entity List. Three hair-products makers — Hetian Haolin Hair Accessories, the Lop County Hair Product Industrial Park and Lop County Meixin Hair Products — have been on the list since June 21, 2022, so their goods, and goods made wholly or in part in Xinjiang, are presumed made with forced labor and are barred unless CBP grants an exception.

changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies cover every Chapter 67 line
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on all products of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84): 12.5% for China, Vietnam, Thailand and the Philippines, 10% for Indonesia, India, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Cambodia, Mexico and Canada. No Chapter 67 line is on the general exemption list (U.S. note 52(b)) or on any country exception list (note 52(j)). EU goods pay 10% in total and Japanese and Korean goods 12.5% in total; USMCA-qualifying goods are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94). Myanmar is not one of the 60. Because most hair and wig lines are Free, the duty is the whole tariff on them.

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on products of Brazil
changes.detail: 25% on goods of Brazil (9903.05.01) on all 13 Chapter 67 lines; none is on the note 50(a)(ii) exemption list. From July 24 the 12.5% 2026 action (9903.05.27) is added.

changes.title: Braiding-hair exclusion order: enforcement case closed
changes.detail: The ITC ended the enforcement proceeding it had opened in January 2026 against one respondent after the complainant withdrew. In April 2026 CBP had ruled that the respondent's redesigned braiding hair is not covered by the order (HQ H355307, affirmed June 17, 2026).

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims (SPI S) still apply.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026. No Chapter 67 line was on the product exemption list (9903.03.03), so wigs, hair, artificial flowers and feather goods all paid it. USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico were exempt.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China, Brazil, India and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. The 9903.01.xx and 9903.02.xx headings are still printed in Revision 21 but are no longer in effect.

changes.title: Extra 25% on products of India ended
changes.detail: Executive Order 14384 ended the additional 25% duty on products of India (9903.01.84) that had applied since August 27, 2025. India's 25% reciprocal duty continued until February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Nicaragua Section 301 tariff phases in from 2027
changes.detail: USTR's action on Nicaragua adds a duty on all Nicaraguan goods that do not originate under CAFTA-DR (9903.89.01): 0% in 2026, 10% from January 1, 2027 and 15% from January 1, 2028. It reaches all 13 Chapter 67 lines; CAFTA-DR-originating goods are not covered.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14357 lowered the IEEPA duty on products of China (9903.01.24) from 20% to 10%. Chinese synthetic wigs then paid 10% + 10% reciprocal + 7.5% List 4A. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Exclusion order on certain pre-stretched synthetic braiding hair
changes.detail: After a Section 337 patent case (337-TA-1415), the ITC issued a limited exclusion order barring entry of infringing pre-stretched synthetic braiding hair (6704.19) and its packaging imported by or for five defaulting respondents, plus cease and desist orders. It is a patent remedy, not a tariff: other importers' goods and non-infringing designs are not covered.

changes.title: Extra 25% on products of India
changes.detail: Executive Order 14329 added 25% on Indian goods (9903.01.84) on top of the 25% reciprocal rate, so Indian human hair and wigs paid 50%. Ended February 7, 2026.

changes.title: Country-specific reciprocal rates replace the 10% baseline
changes.detail: Executive Order 14326 set each country's reciprocal rate: Myanmar +40% (9903.02.43); Vietnam and Bangladesh +20%; Indonesia, Thailand, Cambodia, the Philippines and Pakistan +19%; India +25%; EU, Japanese and Korean goods 15% in total. No Chapter 67 line was on the reciprocal-tariff exemption list. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Canada additional duty raised to 35%
changes.detail: Raised the IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods to +35% (9903.01.10). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty cut from 125% to 10%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14298 cut the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 10% for goods entered from May 14, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty raised to 125%; other country rates paused
changes.detail: Executive Order 14266 raised the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 125% and paused the higher country rates for other countries, leaving the 10% baseline. With the 20% fentanyl duty and List 4A, Chinese synthetic wigs paid 152.5% until May 13, 2025.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff on products of all countries
changes.detail: 10% baseline (9903.01.25) from April 5, 2025 and country rates (9903.02.xx); Canada and Mexico excluded. Hair and wigs, Free at the general rate, paid it in full. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty raised to 20%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14228 raised the IEEPA duty on products of China from 10% to 20%, on top of Lists 3 and 4A. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.01) from March 4, 2025; USMCA-qualifying goods exempt. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Canada
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.10) from March 4, 2025, later raised to +35%; USMCA-qualifying goods exempt. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of China
changes.detail: +10% on all goods of China (9903.01.20) from February 4, 2025, on top of the List 3 and 4A duties. Ended February 24, 2026.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 67 goods fell from **$2.60B in 2024 to $2.14B in 2025** (-17.6%), well below the 2022 peak of $3.69B. Two product families make up almost all of it: **artificial flowers** (6702, $1.07B) — plastic flowers $590M and flowers of other materials $480M — and **wigs, extensions and eyelashes** (6704, $1.04B): human-hair goods $474M (down 38%), synthetic hairpieces and extensions $430M and synthetic complete wigs $105M. Worked hair ($14.8M) and feather goods ($13.0M) are small.

**China supplied 74%** ($1.58B, down 22%): 94% of artificial flowers and 54% of wigs and hair goods. The rest is wigs from South and Southeast Asia and West Africa: Indonesia $172M (down 18%), **Bangladesh $149M (up 14.5%)**, Vietnam $89.3M (up 19.7%) and Senegal $50.4M. India ships mainly worked human hair; Cambodia's wigs and flowers nearly tripled to $13.4M. Myanmar, reported by Comtrade at $3.1M, is small in this data.

Through 2025 China paid List 3 or 4A plus the IEEPA duties (up to 145% more in April–May 2025), and most other suppliers paid the IEEPA reciprocal tariff from April 2025 (Indonesia 19%, Bangladesh and Vietnam 20%, Myanmar 40% from August 7). Those duties ended on February 24, 2026; since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5% applies instead. 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data.

The total rate on Chapter 67 goods depends far more on **where they come from** than on what they are. tariffEngineering.h1: Importing Wigs, Human Hair, Artificial Flowers & Feathers (HTS Ch. 67): Rules, Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Wigs, Hair Extensions & Feathers: Wild-Bird Feather Ban, Forced-Labor Rules & Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 67) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The CBP, FWS and USDA rules for each HTS Chapter 67 line — the wild-bird feather ban, Migratory Bird Treaty Act permits, APHIS rules for bird skins, forced-labor orders on Xinjiang hair products, the braiding-hair exclusion order, origin marking — and the legal ways to pay less: origin, classification, USMCA, FTAs, rulings and drawback.

tariffEngineering.intro:
Chapter 67 goods meet **wildlife and forced-labor rules alongside the duty**. Feathers and skins of wild birds may not be imported at all — raw, processed or as part of another article — except feathers of domesticated species such as chickens, ducks, geese, turkeys and ostriches; migratory-bird feathers need a **Fish and Wildlife Service permit**, and bird skins from regions with avian influenza or Newcastle disease fall under **APHIS** rules. Hair products from three Xinjiang producers are under **CBP withhold release orders** and on the **UFLPA Entity List**, and some pre-stretched synthetic braiding hair is barred by an ITC patent exclusion order.

The ways to pay less are in the schedule: know the **country of origin** of the hair (it follows where the hair was prepared, not where it was sewn), classify **human hair vs. synthetic fiber** and the **flower material** correctly, claim **USMCA** on goods made in Mexico or Canada, claim an **FTA** where the base rate is the cost, get a **binding ruling** and claim **drawback** on re-exports. Each depends on a document, listed below with its regulation.

levers.title: Know the country of origin of hair goods: it follows the hair
levers.saves: The difference between two countries' extra duty — for human-hair wigs and extensions 12.5% (China) vs. 10% (India, Indonesia) vs. nothing extra (Myanmar); for synthetic wigs 20% (China) vs. 10%–12.5% elsewhere
levers.appliesTo: Wigs, extensions, wefts and other articles of human hair (6704.20) and worked hair (6703.00) made in one country from hair prepared in another
levers.document: Production records showing where the hair was collected, cleaned, dyed and sorted and where the article was made; a country-of-origin ruling for a new supply chain.
levers.caveat: CBP found that Indian hair dyed in China and made into wigs and extensions there stays of Indian origin (NY N349850), and that Chinese hair made into tape-in extensions in Indonesia stays Chinese (NY N354172): sewing, gluing and taping are simple assembly. Origin is not a way around the forced-labor rules.

citations.label: CBP ruling NY N349850 (Indian hair made into wigs in China: origin India)
CBP ruling NY N354172 (Chinese hair made into extensions in Indonesia: origin China)

levers.title: Classify by material: human hair, synthetic fiber or other
levers.saves: From China, 7.5 points: human-hair wigs and extensions (6704.20) are not on List 4A and pay 12.5%; synthetic wigs, hairpieces and eyelashes (6704.11, 6704.19) and other materials (6704.90) pay 20%. From Canada, 6704.19 carries the 50% Section 338 duty and 6704.20 does not
levers.appliesTo: Wigs, extensions, wefts, closures, false eyelashes and hairpieces (6704.11–6704.90)
levers.document: Fiber content of the hair (human, synthetic such as modacrylic or polyester, or animal hair such as mink or horsehair), declared on the invoice; a ruling for blends.
levers.caveat: The material must be stated truthfully; a blend is classified by the material that gives it its essential character. Synthetic eyelashes are 6704.19 (NY N293065), human-hair wefts and wigs 6704.20 (NY N305621).

citations.label: CBP ruling NY N305621 (human-hair wefts, closures, wigs, extensions: 6704.20)
CBP ruling NY N293065 (synthetic magnetic eyelashes: 6704.19)
CBP ruling NY N352618 (synthetic braided and dreadlock extensions: 6704.19)

levers.title: Classify artificial flowers by material and construction
levers.saves: Base rates from 3.4% to 17%: plastic flowers assembled by binding or gluing 8.4% (6702.10.20), other plastic flowers and parts 3.4% (6702.10.40), feather flowers 4.7%, man-made-fiber (polyester "silk") flowers 9% (6702.90.35), other materials such as real silk, cotton or paper 17% (6702.90.65). From China, 6702.90.10 and .65 also pay List 4A (+7.5%)
levers.appliesTo: Artificial flowers, foliage, fruit, wreaths, garlands and artificial plants (6702)
levers.document: A product description stating the material of the flowers and foliage and how they are put together (bound with wire or tape, glued, or molded in one piece).
levers.caveat: Chapter 67 note 3 sends flowers of glass to chapter 70 and one-piece molded or carved flowers of pottery, stone, metal or wood out of 6702. Polyester petals were classified in 6702.90.35 (NY N358275) and plastic wreaths in 6702.10.20 (NY N364270).

citations.label: CBP ruling NY N358275 (polyester flower petals: 6702.90.35)
CBP ruling NY N364270 (decorative artificial wreath: 6702.10.20)

levers.title: Claim USMCA on goods made in Mexico or Canada
levers.saves: The 10% Section 301 duty for Mexico or Canada plus the base rate (up to 17%)
levers.appliesTo: All 13 lines, for goods that qualify as originating under USMCA
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, in any format. Headings 6702–6704 need only a change from another heading (General Note 11), so wigs made from imported worked hair (6703) and flowers made from imported fabric qualify; feather articles may be made from imported feathers.
levers.caveat: For Canada, USMCA does not remove the 50% Section 338 duty on 6704.19 (U.S. note 51(a)). The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

levers.appliesTo: Feathers and down (6701) and artificial flowers (6702) from Australia, Bahrain, Chile, Colombia, Israel, Jordan, Korea, Morocco, Oman, Panama, Peru, Singapore, CAFTA-DR and CBERA countries, and AGOA countries (through December 31, 2026)
levers.document: Proof of origin under the program and the SPI on the entry line (AU, BH, CL, CO, IL, JO, KR, MA, OM, PA, PE, SG, P, E or D).
levers.caveat: FTA claims do not remove the 2026 Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(a)); Korea then pays 12.5% in total. GSP (A*) has been expired since December 31, 2020. Hair and wig lines are already Free, so an FTA saves nothing there.

levers.title: Get a binding ruling before you import
levers.saves: Certainty where the line decides the rate: human hair vs. synthetic (12.5% vs. 20% from China); worked hair (6703) vs. unworked hair (0501); feather articles (6701) vs. raw feathers (0505) or goods merely trimmed with feathers; the five artificial-flower lines
levers.appliesTo: Any line where classification or origin is in doubt
levers.document: A ruling request to CBP describing the product, its materials and construction (19 CFR part 177). Published rulings such as N306080 (feather boas, 6701.00.30), N352618 (synthetic extensions), N305621 (human-hair wigs) and N349850 (origin of hair goods) show how CBP decides.
levers.caveat: Rulings apply to the transaction described; a different product may need its own.

levers.title: Claim drawback when the goods are exported
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the duties paid, including Section 301 duties, on imported goods re-exported or used in exported goods
levers.appliesTo: All lines, when the imported goods or substitutes are exported or used in manufacturing exported goods
levers.document: A drawback claim filed in ACE within 5 years of import, with records linking the import to the export.
levers.caveat: Only duties actually paid are refunded; manufacturing drawback needs a ruling or a general manufacturing ruling.

rules.title: Feathers and skins of any bird may not be imported — raw or processed, whole or in part, loose or forming part of another article — except feathers of chickens, turkeys, guineas, geese, ducks, pigeons, ostriches, rheas, English ring-necked pheasants and peafowl that are not wild birds, imports for scientific or educational use, fully manufactured fishing flies and live birds; small quotas of jungle-fowl, mandarin-duck and pheasant skins for fly-tying or millinery need an FWS permit

Feathers and parts of birds on the Migratory Bird Treaty Act list need an FWS migratory-bird import permit; feathers of lawfully taken migratory waterfowl may be used commercially for pillows and similar goods

Feathers, skins and other parts of wild birds are wildlife: declare them to FWS (Form 3-177) at a designated port, hold an import/export license for commercial shipments, and get CITES documents for listed species; wildlife taken or exported in violation of foreign law is barred (Lacey Act)

Bird skins, trophies and other parts of bird carcasses from regions with Newcastle disease or highly pathogenic avian influenza enter only under APHIS conditions (certificate of origin from a free region, or handling at an approved establishment). Raw feathers not further worked than cleaned are classified in heading 0505, not Chapter 67

Wool and hair of ruminants or swine (for example yak or goat hair prepared for wigs) enter freely if scoured, washed or dyed or from a region free of foot-and-mouth disease; otherwise they go to an approved establishment. Human hair is not covered

Goods made with forced labor are barred. CBP withhold release orders cover hair products of Hetian Haolin Hair Accessories (May 2020), Lop County Meixin Hair Product Co. (June 2020) and the Lop County Hair Product Industrial Park (September 2020); all three are on the UFLPA Entity List, and any goods made wholly or in part in Xinjiang are presumed barred unless the importer rebuts the presumption

groups.label: Bird skins with feathers, prepared feathers and down, and articles of feathers or down (boas, fans, trims)
groups.note: Only feathers of domesticated species (chickens, ducks, geese, turkeys, ostriches, pigeons, guineas, rheas, ring-necked pheasants, peafowl) may be imported commercially; wild-bird feathers are barred and migratory-bird feathers need an FWS permit. Bird skins from avian-influenza regions fall under APHIS rules. From China, List 3 adds 25%.

groups.label: Artificial flowers, foliage and fruit and their parts; articles made of them (wreaths, garlands, artificial plants)
groups.note: Flowers made with real feathers (6702.90.10) are subject to the wild-bird feather ban. The rate turns on the material: plastic 3.4% or 8.4%, man-made fibers 9%, other 17%. From China, feather and "other" flowers also pay List 4A.

groups.label: Human hair, dressed, bleached or otherwise worked; wool, animal hair or textile fibers prepared for wigs
groups.note: Worked human hair is Free at the general rate; the extra duty by country is the whole tariff. Hair from three Xinjiang producers is barred under withhold release orders and the UFLPA. Russian human hair pays 35% in place of column 2.

groups.label: Wigs, hair extensions, false eyelashes and beards, switches and the like, of synthetic fibers, human hair or other materials
groups.note: Free at the general rate on every line. The forced-labor bars on Xinjiang hair reach wigs and extensions made from it; certain pre-stretched synthetic braiding hair is under an ITC exclusion order. Canadian 6704.19 pays 50% Section 338 duty even with USMCA.

faqs.question: What is the HTS code for wigs?
searchedAs: hs code for human hair wigs
faqs.answer: Heading 6704. Complete wigs of synthetic fibers are 6704.11.00; wigs, hairpieces and extensions of human hair are 6704.20.00; wigs of other materials such as animal hair are 6704.90.00. All are Free at the general rate, so the extra duty for the country of origin is the whole tariff: from China 20% on synthetic wigs and 12.5% on human-hair wigs.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for hair extensions and hair weave?
searchedAs: hs code for human hair extensions
hs code for synthetic hair extensions
faqs.answer: Extensions, wefts, closures and frontals of human hair are 6704.20.00 (CBP ruling N305621). Synthetic extensions, braiding hair and hairpieces other than complete wigs are 6704.19.00 (N352618). Both are Free at the general rate. From China, 6704.19 pays 20% and 6704.20 pays 12.5%; from Canada, 6704.19 pays the 50% Section 338 duty even with USMCA.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for false eyelashes?
faqs.answer: Heading 6704 names eyelashes. Synthetic-fiber lashes are 6704.19.00 (CBP ruling N293065 for magnetic lashes), human-hair lashes 6704.20.00 and lashes of animal hair such as mink 6704.90.00. All are Free at the general rate; from China synthetic and mink lashes pay 20% (12.5% + 7.5% List 4A), from Indonesia 10%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for human hair?
searchedAs: us hts code for human hair
faqs.answer: Human hair that has been dressed, thinned, bleached or otherwise worked is 6703.00.30; wool, animal hair or textile fibers prepared for making wigs are 6703.00.60. Raw, unworked human hair is 0501.00.00 (Chapter 5). Worked hair is Free at the general rate; from China it pays 20% (List 4A + 12.5%), from India 10%, and from Russia 35% in place of column 2 plus 12.5%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for artificial flowers?
searchedAs: hs tariff code for artificial flowers
faqs.answer: Heading 6702. Plastic flowers assembled by binding or gluing are 6702.10.20 (8.4%) and other plastic flowers and parts 6702.10.40 (3.4%); flowers of feathers are 6702.90.10 (4.7%), of man-made fibers such as polyester "silk" 6702.90.35 (9%) and of other materials 6702.90.65 (17%). Wreaths and garlands of artificial flowers are classified here too.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for feathers and feather boas?
faqs.answer: Worked feathers, down, bird skins with their feathers and articles of them are 6701: articles such as boas, fans and trims 6701.00.30, other 6701.00.60, both 4.7%. CBP classified turkey-feather boas in 6701.00.30 (N306080). Feathers only cleaned, disinfected or preserved are 0505, bedding filled with down is 9404, and from China 6701 pays 42.2%.

faqs.question: What are the tariffs on wigs from China?
searchedAs: tariffs on wigs from china to usa
faqs.answer: Synthetic wigs, hairpieces and extensions (6704.11, 6704.19) and wigs of other materials (6704.90) pay 20%: List 4A 7.5% (9903.88.15) plus 12.5% under the 2026 Section 301 action (9903.05.31). Human-hair wigs and extensions (6704.20) were only on the suspended List 4B, so they pay 12.5%. The 2025 IEEPA duties, which took Chinese wigs to as much as 152.5%, ended February 24, 2026.

faqs.question: Are there tariffs on hair extensions?
searchedAs: are there tariffs on hair extensions
human hair extensions import duty rates
faqs.answer: The general rate is Free, but since July 24, 2026 the Section 301 tariff on 60 economies applies: 10% from Indonesia, India and Bangladesh, 12.5% from Vietnam and the Philippines, 12.5% (human hair) or 20% (synthetic) from China. Myanmar is not one of the 60, so its extensions enter Free. USMCA-qualifying extensions from Mexico pay nothing.

faqs.question: What is the import duty on artificial flowers?
searchedAs: us import duty on artificial flowers
how to import artificial flowers from china
faqs.answer: The base rate is 3.4%–17% by material, plus the country's extra duty. From China: plastic flowers 15.9% or 20.9%, polyester flowers 21.5%, feather flowers 24.7% and other-material flowers 37% (they also pay List 4A). From Vietnam or Thailand the base rate plus 12.5%; from EU countries 10% in total (17% for 6702.90.65).

faqs.question: Can you import feathers into the United States?
faqs.answer: Only feathers of domesticated birds — chickens, turkeys, guineas, geese, ducks, pigeons, ostriches, rheas, English ring-necked pheasants and peafowl that are not wild — may be imported commercially. Feathers and skins of other birds are barred, raw or processed, even as part of another article (HTSUS Chapter 5 note 1, 19 CFR 12.29), with exceptions for science, education and fishing flies. Migratory-bird feathers need an FWS permit.

faqs.question: Can I import hair products from China?
faqs.answer: Yes, but hair products made by Hetian Haolin Hair Accessories, Lop County Meixin Hair Products or in the Lop County Hair Product Industrial Park are under CBP withhold release orders and on the UFLPA Entity List, and any goods made wholly or in part in Xinjiang are presumed made with forced labor and barred. Other Chinese hair goods pay 12.5%–20% extra.

faqs.question: What do HS codes 6704.11, 6704.19 and 6704.20 mean?
faqs.answer: 6704.11 is complete wigs of synthetic textile materials, 6704.19 other synthetic articles (hairpieces, extensions, braiding hair, eyelashes), 6704.20 wigs and articles of human hair, and 6704.90 the same goods of other materials such as animal hair. All four are Free at the general rate; 6704.20 is the only one not on China's List 4A.

faqs.question: How many wigs and artificial flowers does the U.S. import, and from where?
faqs.answer: $2.14B of Chapter 67 goods in 2025, down 17.6% from $2.60B. Artificial flowers were $1.07B and wigs, extensions and eyelashes $1.04B. China supplied 74% (94% of the flowers), followed by Indonesia ($172M), Bangladesh ($149M), Vietnam ($89.3M) and Senegal ($50.4M), almost all wigs and hair goods.
